definition: In artificial intelligence (AI), commonsense reasoning is a human-like ability to make presumptions about the type and essence of ordinary situations humans encounter every day.
details: These assumptions include judgments about the nature of physical objects, taxonomic properties, and peoples' intentions. A device that exhibits commonsense reasoning might be capable of drawing conclusions that are similar to humans' folk psychology (humans' innate ability to reason about people's behavior and intentions) and naive physics (humans' natural understanding of the physical world).
story: Imagine a mathematician who writes every step on paper, reads it back, crosses out a bad line, and starts that line over. Slowing down to think often beats answering fast. Instead of blurting out an answer, the machine talks its way through the problem one step at a time. More time spent reconsidering can be worth more than a bigger model. And that habit of thinking twice — or a hundred times — is Commonsense reasoning.
